results.title: Nebius at Goldman Sachs conference: demand stays ahead of supply By Investing.com
highlights:
- Nebius said customer demand now extends into Q1 and Q2 2028, with some clients seeking tens of thousands of vGPUs and GPUs.
- Management said four major customer wins averaged about $1 billion each and were won on technical performance and reliability, not price.
- A recent auction for Blackwell capacity produced prices 15% to 20% above prior list rates, showing strong pricing power.
- The company is expanding beyond AI-native customers into enterprise accounts, helped by a new partnership with Palantir.
- Nebius is also building an asset-light growth model with infrastructure partners to ease limits on physical buildout and capital.

...

- He said demand is growing “times a year, if not tens of times a year,” while physical infrastructure cannot expand at that pace.
- Nebius said it now has visibility into demand for 24 months or more, up from an earlier 18-month view.
- Customers are already ordering capacity for Q1 and Q2 2028.
- Management said it could sell all of its 2027 capacity today if it chose to pre-sell it.
- The company described demand as “unlimited” from a visible perspective, with the main constraint being build capacity and financing.

...

## Pricing power and auction strategy

Nebius said it has begun using auctions to set prices for scarce capacity, starting with Blackwell processors about a month before the conference.

- The first auction delivered prices 15% to 20% above earlier list rates, after manual price increases had already been made.
- Management said both Nebius and the winning customers preferred the auction format because it guaranteed allocation.
- The company plans to extend the auction model to a larger self-serve customer base with hundreds of thousands of clients.
- Auction prices will serve as a baseline for future discounts and upsells, depending on customer needs.

Volozh said manual price increases alone are not enough when demand is this strong, making auctions a better way to discover market-clearing prices.

...

It grows, let’s say, times a year, if not tens of times a year. The physical world is limited. It cannot grow 10 times a year. That’s why we have this imbalance. We probably have said that a couple of months ago, that if we wanted, we could sell all the 2027 demand today. We have much more ask than we can physically serve. We do not pre-sell much. We are focusing on free capacity, which we will be selling later. We’re building capacity which will be sold later. But since we last publicly spoke, actually this sign of this demand went even further. Now we receive orders for first, second quarter of 2028. People are demanding tens of thousands of vGPUs and GPUs now. So we see demand today as unlimited.

...

Arkady Volozh, Chief Executive Officer, Nebius: Well, when you have this imbalance between demand and supply, the best price discovery mechanism is something like an auction in one way or another. We tried to do it manually first to raise the prices. It did not help. The demand is still there. What is the best mechanism to discover what the real price balance should be? We ran our first experimental auction for the Blackwell processors a month ago, several weeks ago. We achieved results when we got 15%-20% higher price than we ever sold before, after all our price raises. We liked the experience. More importantly, our clients liked the experience. The guys who won this auction, they tweeted that they are happy that they were able to get guaranteed capacity through this mechanism.

This is the only way when there is a deficit of resources and you need it, what is the way to get it guaranteed? Go in price competition and win. They won the auction, and they were happy about it, and we are happy about it, and probably it is the right way to find this right balance. We will do more of this. We are told that we will put more capacity on the auction. We now will start experimenting with our longer tail clients, self-serve clients. We have hundreds of thousands of clients which are self-served. Small client with preemptive mechanisms. We will go introduce something like the auction there. Probably this is the right mechanism to actually work with more regular and bigger clients.

At least we should use some mechanism like the auction to discover the price, and then based on this price discovery, we should offer them discounts or upsell from that prices depending on different circumstances for these clients. Auctioning is the best way to find the right balance in this supply-demand situation, which we are now in.

results.title: Nebius Group (NBIS) Transcript: Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference
highlights:
Supply and demand is a well-known problem now, and it's a good problem to have because demand exceeds supply significantly today. That's because AI found a lot of niches to grow and to bring new value, to generate value, and these niches are growing exponentially. Whereas infrastructure supply is grounded in the real world, and it cannot multiply this fast. You cannot make physical things 10 times more a year of physical things. It's not software which you can multiply very quickly. So supply is scarce, demand is growing, and the situation, at least for now, is getting, I don't know, worse or better. More and more severe. There is more and more demand, and unfortunately, with all this growth in infrastructure, it's not enough to cope with growing demand. So the difference is increasing. And it all reflects in prices, in the whole waterfall of pricing.

 Prices go up, and we can see it. You can see it on all the expert management systems. Prices are going up. In our business, we just reported last quarter that we started selling like everybody else, bare metal prices were at the level of 10, maybe $15 million per megawatt. We realized that demand is much higher. We tried manually to adjust this pricing, and until we found the next level of $20, $25 million per megawatt for consumer level, retail level. And on even shorter contracts, the demand is even more higher. There's the people who need capacity now, not ready to wait until it's available in 2027, 2028, and they're ready to pay much higher, $40, $50 million per megawatt for these shorter-term contracts. This is what we discovered, not only we as an industry, we as a company as well discovered this year.

 We discovered that kind of manually, and we understood that on this disproportionate market where demand is high and supply is not enough, the best way for price discovery to balance it through the price, you need some automated procedure to always balance growing demand versus limited supply. We were among the first, I think, who went to develop this system of auctions. We first experimented. Again, it's why we were able to do it, because in the past, for the previous 20 years, we worked on consumer markets of internet advertising or transportation services and all those industries, consumer industries, they're all balanced by some kind of auctioning systems. Both advertising, surge pricing in Uber, taxi business, and many, many areas. The balance, it's huge industries, and the balances in those industries are all found in some kind of auctioning systems. They're not just simple auctions.

...

It is a question of optimization and de-risking. Of course, it is great to put everything on short-term auction, try to sell everything at $50, $60 per megawatt. If something happens, then it happens. You have nothing. We divide our customers in three big buckets. Our main business is in the middle back bucket, where we have, let us say, mid-range customers, people who buy thousands and tens of thousands of GPUs for one, two, three years. This is our sweet spot, and this is our main market. We have dozens and hundreds of companies who are there. This is our target market, but to serve it, you need to have capacity to sell. We had to start with a different sector. We became famous for our contracts with Meta and Microsoft, which is great contracts, great customers, profitable, and so on.

results.title: Nebius at Citi’s 2026 Global TMT Conference: growth meets capital strain By Investing.com
highlights:
Volozh said pricing improved sharply during 2024 as demand outpaced supply. He said bare metal services were initially priced at about $10 million to $15 million per megawatt, then rose to $20 million to $25 million per megawatt for consumer or retail-level capacity. For shorter contracts, he said customers were willing to pay $40 million to $50 million per megawatt.

That pricing discovery led Nebius to use auctions to allocate capacity. Volozh said manual price adjustments were not enough, and the company needed a more dynamic system to match scarce supply with urgent demand. He compared the approach with auction systems used in consumer markets such as advertising and transportation.

...

Volozh said the AI infrastructure market remains extremely tight. He said demand is growing quickly because AI is finding new uses across industries, while physical supply is constrained by real-world limits such as power, land, permitting and construction timelines.

“Supply and demand is a well-known problem now, and it’s a good problem to have because demand exceeds supply significantly today,” he said. “That’s because AI found a lot of niches to grow and to bring new value, to generate value, and these niches are growing exponentially.”

He said the company had to move from fixed pricing to auction-based allocation because customers were willing to pay very different amounts depending on urgency. Some customers need capacity now and cannot wait until 2027 or 2028, he said, which pushes prices higher for shorter-term contracts.

Volozh estimated that the current pricing environment could last 18 to 24 months, though he said the timing depends on whether AI continues to create value fast enough to keep demand elevated. He also said the market could eventually normalize as more supply comes online.

results.title: Nebius CEO Volozh estimates $250 billion in capex spend by 2030 - Blockspace
results.author: William Foxley
highlights:
Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) CEO Arkady Volozh said Wednesday that deploying 5 GW of contracted AI infrastructure capacity through 2030 would require about $250 billion of financing. Nebius has financed roughly 20% of that amount, leaving approximately $200 billion to raise.

Speaking with Tyler Radke, Citi’s co-head of U.S. Software, at the Citi Global TMT Conference, Volozh identified financing and construction as the main challenges facing the buildout. “So far, we financed maybe 20% of that,” he said. His estimate implies a cost of roughly $50 million per MW across data centers, GPUs and supporting infrastructure.

...

In August, the company priced $5 billion of convertible notes with senior unsecured status, including $3 billion of 0.50% notes due 2030 and $2 billion of 4.50% notes due 2034.

...

That asset-level loan, backed by deployed GPUs and cash flows from a customer with an investment-grade rating, carries interest at one-month Term SOFR plus 250 bps and matures in October 2030.

Nebius ended the second quarter with $8 billion of cash and cash equivalents after raising approximately $2.8 billion through its at-the-market equity program. It expects customer prepayments of more than $9 billion in 2026, while second-quarter contracts covered 50% to 60% of associated capex through upfront payments.

...

## Current contract pricing supports rapid payback

Volozh said one-to-three-year contracts are generating approximately $20 million to $25 million of revenue per MW. Shorter agreements for customers seeking immediate capacity can reach $40 million to $50 million per MW, supporting Nebius’ stated 22-month capex payback period at current prices.

Nebius said second-quarter revenue reached $582 million, up 454% from a year earlier, and retained 2026 capex guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion. Volozh cautioned that current pricing would decline as supply catches up with demand.

Nebius expects connected power to reach 800 MW to 1 GW by year-end and plans to add over 1 GW of new capacity in 2027. Before that capacity can generate revenue, it must be commissioned, fitted with GPU clusters and integrated into Nebius’ cloud platform.

results.title: Neocloud Companies Cut Data Center Payback to 2 Years With GPU Price Hikes | Gate News
results.author: GateAiHorizon
highlights:
- CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN raised GPU prices significantly during Q2, with CoreWeave implementing 25% increases.
- Data center investment payback periods fell from 4-5 years to approximately 2 years due to price increases.
- Google reported over 500 companies consuming more than 1 trillion tokens during Q2 conference call.

Global neocloud companies emphasized GPU pricing increases during Q2 earnings announcements, with data center investment payback periods shortening from the previous 4-5 years to around 2 years, according to analysis by Korea Investment & Securities. The pricing surge stems from rapid growth in enterprise token consumption, suggesting similar changes may eventually affect Korean data center operators. Neocloud refers to service providers offering GPU-based cloud computing specialized for artificial intelligence model training and inference.

## CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN Announce GPU Pricing Increases

Korea Investment & Securities researchers Jung Ho-yoon and Hwang In-jun stated in a report that neocloud companies uniformly emphasized GPU pricing increases during Q2 conference calls. CoreWeave, the leading neocloud company, implemented a 25% price increase across all products in July. Nebius announced that capacity sold at its Q2 auction achieved prices 15% higher than the previous peak. IREN reported that 3-year contract unit prices increased 125% compared to last November, while 5-year contract prices rose 70%.

## Data Center Payback Periods Drop to Under 2 Years

The price increases are directly improving profitability metrics. Nebius stated that investment payback would take less than 2 years at prices exceeding $20 million per megawatt. IREN disclosed signing a 3-year contract at $20 million per MW, with recent contract discussions reaching $25 million per MW. The researchers noted that the data center industry, which previously required 4-5 years for investment recovery based on 5-year contracts, has reached a level where investment payback is achievable through 3-year contracts due to unit price increases.

...

Major neocloud companies cited increased inference demand as the reason for pricing increases. During its Q2 conference call, Google reported over 500 companies consuming more than 1 trillion tokens and over 2,000 companies consuming more than 100 billion tokens. Microsoft announced that the number of customers reaching 1 trillion annual token consumption increased 400% year-over-year. Model developers like Anthropic and OpenAI charge enterprise customers based on token usage, while GPU costs are tied to hourly rates or fixed contracts, creating a structure where revenue grows as enterprise token usage increases.

results.title: Neoclod GPU Prices Surge 25% in Q2, Data Center ROI Period Shrinks to 2 Years | Gate News
results.author: GateNews
highlights:
According to Korea Investment & Securities analysts on August 1, neoclod companies reported significant GPU rental fee increases in Q2 results. CoreWeave implemented a 25% price increase across all products in July, while Nebius saw capacity auction prices 15% higher than previous highs. IREN's three-year contract rates jumped 125% versus November 2025, with five-year rates up 70%. Consequentially, data center investment payback periods have compressed from the traditional 4-5 years to under 2 years, with Nebius noting that $20 million per megawatt (MW) contracts now enable sub-two-year ROI, and IREN citing recent $25 million per MW agreements in negotiation.

Analysts attribute the surge to accelerating token consumption by enterprises. Google disclosed in Q2 that over 500 companies now consume 1 trillion-plus tokens, with 2,000+ consuming 100 billion tokens. Microsoft reported a 400% year-over-year increase in customers reaching annual token consumption of 1 trillion, driving higher profitability for AI model developers and intensifying data center pricing pressure.

results.title: Nebius en la conferencia TMT global de Citi 2026: crecimiento y presión de capital  Por Investing.com
highlights:
Volozh señaló que los precios mejoraron notablemente durante 2024 a medida que la demanda superó a la oferta. Indicó que los servicios de metal desnudo se fijaron inicialmente en torno a 10 millones a 15 millones de dólares por megavatio, para luego subir a 20 millones a 25 millones de dólares por megavatio para capacidad de consumo o nivel minorista. Para contratos de menor duración, afirmó que los clientes estaban dispuestos a pagar entre 40 millones y 50 millones de dólares por megavatio.

Ese descubrimiento de precios llevó a Nebius a utilizar subastas para asignar capacidad. Volozh señaló que los ajustes manuales de precios no eran suficientes y que la Empresa necesitaba un sistema más dinámico para hacer coincidir una oferta escasa con una demanda urgente. Comparó este enfoque con los sistemas de subasta utilizados en mercados de consumo como la publicidad y el transporte.

...

Señaló que la Empresa tuvo que pasar de precios fijos a una asignación basada en subastas porque los clientes estaban dispuestos a pagar cantidades muy diferentes según la urgencia. Algunos clientes necesitan capacidad ahora y no pueden esperar hasta 2027 o 2028, afirmó, lo que eleva los precios para los contratos a más corto plazo.

Volozh estimó que el entorno de precios actual podría durar entre 18 y 24 meses, aunque señaló que el momento depende de si la inteligencia artificial sigue creando valor con suficiente rapidez como para mantener la demanda elevada. También indicó que el mercado podría eventualmente normalizarse a medida que entre en línea más oferta.
